# Scholar-Kit under Codex

This file is what Codex reads. Everything below the next rule is the kit's
constitution, copied verbatim from `CLAUDE.md`; it binds a Codex session exactly
as it binds a Claude Code one. The constitution, the skills and the agent files
were written in Claude Code's vocabulary. Read them with this table:

| The text says | Under Codex |
|---|---|
| `/outline`, `/draft methods`, any `/command` | the skill of the same name: `$outline`, `$draft methods`. Whatever follows the name is the argument the skill's text calls `<section>`, `[--flag]`, etc. |
| "dispatch `literature-scout`", "the X agent", "subagent" | spawn the custom agent whose name is X (`.codex/agents/X.toml`) and wait for its result. If that agent type is not available in this session, spawn a default agent and give it `.claude/agents/X.md` as its instructions — never do the agent's read-heavy work in this session instead (Invariant 4). |
| Read / Grep / Glob | shell read commands (`cat`, `sed -n`, `rg`, `ls`) |
| Write / Edit / NotebookEdit | `apply_patch` |
| Bash | the shell tool |
| AskUserQuestion, "ask the user", "request approval" | ask in plain text and STOP until the user answers. An approval gate is a real stop, never a question you answer yourself. |
| TodoWrite | `update_plan` |
| WebSearch / WebFetch | the web search tool; fetch a page with it, not from memory |
| `mcp__server__tool` | the same name |
| `claude mcp add …` | `codex mcp add …` |
| "Claude Code", "this session" | this Codex session |

Paths in the text are real. `.claude/` is the authored half: skills, agents,
hooks, settings. What Codex reads is generated from it and must never be edited
by hand — `.agents/skills/` (the same skills, plus the setting that keeps a
command from starting on its own), `.codex/agents/`, `.codex/hooks.json`,
`.codex/rules/` and this file. To change any of them, change the `.claude/`
source and run `python scripts/codex_sync.py --project`. The gates themselves
exist once, in `.claude/hooks/`; `.codex/hooks/codex_adapter.py` only feeds
Codex's `apply_patch` to them.

Three things differ, and they matter:

1. **The gates run only if you trusted them.** Codex skips a hook until the
   user has reviewed it in `/hooks`, and loads `.codex/` only in a trusted
   project. Until then Invariants 3 and 6 are guidance, not gates. If a
   protected file was edited or a draft was written before outline approval
   and nothing stopped it, say so to the user and point them to `/hooks` —
   do not carry on as if the gate had passed.
2. **A read-only agent is read-only by contract and by hook, not by toolset.**
   Codex gives every agent the session's tools. The agent files state the
   contract; `agent_write_scope` enforces it when hooks are trusted.
3. **`.claude/settings.json`'s permission list does not apply.** The
   destructive-command part of it is mirrored in `.codex/rules/scholar-kit.rules`;
   the script-owned-file part is enforced by `protect_data_files`. Reading
   `.env` and key files is not blocked by this kit under Codex — do not read
   them.

`scripts/token_report.py` reads Claude Code transcripts only; it reports
nothing for a Codex session.
